real_simulation_tunnel_modale_title.message: Test a local site on a Live device

real_simulation_tunnel_modale_baseline.message: The Live device runs remotely: it can't see your machine. A tunnel gives your local server a temporary public address for the duration of your tests.

real_simulation_tunnel_linux_note.message: Command for Debian / Ubuntu (x86_64). Other distributions:

real_simulation_tunnel_step_run.message: Start the tunnel to your local server

real_simulation_tunnel_step_paste.message: Copy the tunnel address from the terminal

real_simulation_tunnel_step_paste_note.message: After a few seconds, a “Your quick Tunnel has been created!” box appears. Copy the address inside it, in https://…trycloudflare.com, and paste it into the field on the device.

real_simulation_tunnel_tip_logs.message: The many INF lines around it are normal: they're technical details you can ignore.

real_simulation_tunnel_tip_delay.message: The address may take up to a minute to respond after it's created: if the device shows an error, wait and try again.

real_simulation_tunnel_tip_terminal.message: Keep the terminal open while you test: the tunnel stops when you close it or press Ctrl + C. A new address is generated each time you start it.

real_simulation_tunnel_step_hosts.message: If the page is blocked, allow the tunnel address

real_simulation_tunnel_step_hosts_note.message: Development servers reject unknown host names. With Vite, add this to vite.config; with webpack-dev-server, use allowedHosts: 'all'.

real_simulation_tunnel_free_text.message: Cloudflare Quick Tunnels require no sign-up. The address changes every time you start one, and they're meant for testing, not production.
